messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Pager fired: Dedicated cluster 'nova-care-prod' — tenant=Novacare — high p95 latency and rising 5xx rate. Alert id: PD-98123. Auto-pscal triggered? no.

pagerduty: PD-98123: page fired to group=eng-oncall | severity=critical | runbook: /runbooks/tenant-latency.md | link: https://pd.example/PD-98123

maria_oncall: acked via PagerDuty. I'm on it. Quick check of dashboards now.

sam_sre: thanks. maria, do we have sudden burst or degraded nodes? I see queue depth on reserved-queue up 3x.

maria_oncall: digging. metrics snapshot: p50=120ms p95=2.4s errors=4.5% (baseline ~0.1%). request rate +40% last 5m.

lucas_eng: tagging in — this is Novacare dedicated pool. Their reserved capacity should autoscale up to 60k tok/s. Can we confirm scheduler isn't throttling?

support_ops: Novacare reported "slow responses" to their customers 3m ago. No 503s yet from their side but elevated latency and a few timed-out webhooks.

oncall_backup: @maria_oncall if you need to handoff later I can take next 30m.

maria_oncall: plan: 1) check node health + GPU mem pressure 2) confirm autoscale events 3) enable short-term spillover to shared-hosted pool if needed.

sam_sre: run: ```kubectl -n dedicated-novacare get pods -l pool=novacare -o wide```

lucas_eng: results: 2 pods OOMKilled in last 7m, others with high iowait. Kernel logs show nv_peer_mem warnings on two nodes.

maria_oncall: ok that explains stalled KV cache writes. I'm going to temporarily flip routing policy to allow burst routing to shared-tier (soft-fallback). Doing that now.

maria_oncall: /ops route set --tenant novacare --fallback shared-hosted --max-burst 2000 --reason "evicting to avoid tail latency"

incident-bot: action recorded: routing-policy updated by maria_oncall. OldTraffic -> NovacareDedicated, NewTraffic -> shared-hosted (spill 25%).

sam_sre: metrics after spill: p95 dropped to 900ms, errors down to 2.1%, queue depth halved. Good partial win. Need to remediate node-level memory pressure and kernel warnings.

lucas_eng: I'll SSH into the affected hosts and check nv_peer_mem driver + dmesg. If we can't immediate kernel fix, recommend cordon+recreate the two problem nodes to restore KV cache stability.

support_ops: I've opened support ticket to Novacare with status update: "We detected elevated latency for a subset of requests and have routed a fraction of traffic to fallback capacity while we remediate. No customer data exposure. We'll update every 15 minutes." :spiral_calendar:

maria_oncall: cordon/drain planned for the two hosts. Doing controlled drain to avoid mass evictions. ```for node in node-12 node-14; do kubectl drain $node --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m; done```

incident-bot: PD-98123: acknowledged by maria_oncall. escalation threshold=10m. next escalate to eng-lead if >10m without resolution.

oncall_backup: ping — I'll monitor dashboards and stand by for any customer-impact escalation.

sam_sre: after draining/recreate, we should roll PV-backed cache pods back up with increased `--kv-cache-max-size=6GB` for Novacare for next 1 hour. Also leave spill policy in place until p95 < 500ms for 10m.

lucas_eng: db: recreated node images with nv_peer_mem patched. Nodes back up, pods rescheduled. K/V warm-up in progress ~4m.

maria_oncall: monitoring: p95=420ms, errors=0.3%, queue depth normal. I'm going to start scaling traffic back from the shared-hosted fallback: /ops route adjust --tenant novacare --fallback none --gradual 10pct/30s

incident-bot: PD-98123: status=resolved (mitigated) — root cause: kernel driver nv_peer_mem causing KV cache stalls on 2 hosts -> cascade queueing -> reserved pool latency spike. Postmortem assigned to lucas_eng.

sam_sre: filing short postmortem notes and timeline. Recommend follow-ups: a) add nv_peer_mem healthcheck to node exporter, b) automatic cordon on driver errors, c) review autoscale trigger sensitivity for reserved pools.

support_ops: Novacare updated: "Issue mitigated, routing restored. Thank you for the fast response." :thumbsup:

oncall_backup: nice job team. I'll close PD after 30m if no regression.

maria_oncall: leaving thread, handoff to oncall_backup for 30m watch.

lucas_eng: I'll own the postmortem and include kernel logs + nodes list and remediation script.```#!/bin/bash
for n in node-12 node-14; do ssh $n 'sudo dmesg | tail -n 200' > ${n}-dmesg.log; done```

pagerduty: PD-98123: incident closed by maria_oncall.

incident-bot: note: follow-up ticket created: INF-4567 "nv_peer_mem healthcheck + cordon automation" assigned to lucas_eng."
